tools.name: projects.getMetadata
tools.description: Get the data dictionary (field definitions) for a REDCap project. Returns field names, types, labels, validation, choices, and branching logic. Use this to understand a project's structure before reading or writing records. PROACTIVE USE: when the user describes a concept in natural language ('severity', 'consented', 'enrolled', 'site'), call this tool FIRST and read each candidate's field_label to pick the right field yourself — do NOT ask the user to name the field for you. That is your job. Only ask the user to disambiguate when the top 2 labels are both plausible for their wording AND a wrong pick would be hard to recover from.

fields.description: Optional list of specific field names to retrieve. Omit to get all fields.

tools.name: projects.getInstruments
tools.description: List all instruments (forms) in a REDCap project. Returns instrument machine names and human-readable labels.

tools.name: records.get
tools.description: Retrieve data for a specific record by its record ID. Optionally filter to specific fields or events (for longitudinal projects).

fields.description: Optional list of specific field names to retrieve

events.description: Optional list of event names (for longitudinal projects only)

tools.name: records.search
tools.description: Search records in a REDCap project with an optional REDCap logic filter expression. Returns: total_record_count, a 'reference' id (the FULL result set, cached server-side in the PHP session), and 'preview_markdown' — a ready-made markdown table of the first 20 rows with sensible columns. ALWAYS render preview_markdown verbatim to the user; never ask which fields to show. Raw record rows are withheld by default (keeps context small) — pass include_records=true with a modest limit only when you need raw values for computation. For follow-up questions about the same data, DO NOT start a new search: pass the 'reference' back with a NEW 'filter' to narrow the cached recordset in memory (no database round trip), or with offset/limit to page (each page returns its own preview_markdown). When the user wants to ACCUMULATE ('also add severity 4', 'include those too'), use 'append_to' with the new filter — only the new slice is queried, then merged into the working set. Use REDCap logic syntax for filters, e.g. '[age] > 18'. For pure counts, prefer records.count; for ID-only enumeration, prefer records.listIds. LITERAL AUTO-TRANSLATION: choice labels in your filter (e.g. [d_legal_sex] = "Female") are auto-expanded server-side to OR with the underlying code, so label and code paths both work. When the response includes a 'filter_translations' array, mention briefly to the user what you wrote and what the tool auto-translated (e.g. "I wrote d_legal_sex = 'Female', which the tool expanded to also match code 2"). PROACTIVE FIELD RESOLUTION: if you're not sure which field captures the user's concept, call projects.getMetadata first and pick the field whose field_label matches the user's words. Don't ask the user to name the field for you. UNKNOWN FIELDS: if the filter references fields that don't exist, the response includes a 'suggestions' map keyed by the unknown field name. Each value has a 'best_match' (field name), 'best_label' (its human label), and 'candidates' (up to 3 ranked by combined name+label similarity). Use best_match UNLESS best_label clearly doesn't fit the user's wording — in which case pick from candidates by label. Re-run with the chosen field; tell the user what you substituted and why.

filter.description: REDCap logic filter expression, e.g. '[field_name] > 18'. Omit to match all records. When combined with 'reference', the filter is applied to the cached recordset instead of the database.

reference.description: Reference id from a previous records.search call. Pass it to page through (offset/limit) or narrow (new filter) the cached result set without re-querying.

append_to.description: Reference id from a previous records.search call. When the user wants to ACCUMULATE results ('also show me severity 4', 'add those to the list'), pass append_to + a new filter: only the new slice is queried, then UNIONED into the cached set. Use 'reference' instead when the user wants to narrow or replace the current set.

fields.description: Optional list of specific field names to include in results. Omit to get all fields — recommended, so follow-up filters on any field can be served from cache.

return_format.description: Response format for raw rows (only used when include_records=true)

include_records.description: If true, include raw record rows in the response. Default false — preview_markdown + reference are usually all you need.

limit.description: Max records to return in this call (uncapped — the full result set is cached server-side regardless). Defaults to 500. If total_record_count exceeds ~500, suggest the user narrow their filter or use records.aggregate for whole-dataset questions.

offset.description: Number of matching records to skip, for paging through results beyond the per-call cap.

tools.name: records.count
tools.description: Return the number of records in a REDCap project matching an optional REDCap logic filter. No record data is returned — only the count. Cheap alternative to records.search when the user only wants a count (e.g. 'how many records are there?', 'how many consented?'). LITERAL AUTO-TRANSLATION: choice labels in your filter (e.g. [d_legal_sex] = "Female") are auto-expanded server-side to OR with the underlying code, so label and code paths both work. When the response includes a 'filter_translations' array, mention briefly to the user what you wrote and what the tool auto-translated. PROACTIVE FIELD RESOLUTION: if you're not sure which field captures the user's concept, call projects.getMetadata first and pick the field whose field_label matches the user's words. Don't ask the user to name the field for you. UNKNOWN FIELDS: if the filter references fields that don't exist, the response includes a 'suggestions' map keyed by the unknown field name. Each value has a 'best_match' (field name), 'best_label' (its human label), and 'candidates' (up to 3 ranked by combined name+label similarity). Use best_match UNLESS best_label clearly doesn't fit the user's wording — in which case pick from candidates by label. Re-run with the chosen field; tell the user what you substituted and why.

filter.description: Optional REDCap logic filter, e.g. '[consent] = "1"'. Omit to count all records.

tools.name: records.listIds
tools.description: Return just the record IDs in a REDCap project (no field data). PREFER THIS TOOL over records.search when the user asks for record IDs only, a count of records, or a specific range of record IDs — it returns the same data with much less context cost. Use records.search only when the user wants field values too. Supports the same filter as records.count/records.search. When more than 50 IDs match, the full list is cached server-side in the PHP session and a short reference id is returned; pass that reference back to retrieve a page.

filter.description: Optional REDCap logic filter, e.g. '[consent] = "1"'. Omit to list all record IDs.

reference.description: If a previous call returned a reference, pass it here to retrieve a paginated slice instead of re-querying.

offset.description: For paging through a referenced result. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: Max IDs to return in this call. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: records.evaluateLogic
tools.description: Evaluate a REDCap logic expression against a specific record. Returns true or false. Useful for checking eligibility criteria or branching conditions.

record_id.description: The record ID to evaluate against

logic.description: REDCap logic expression to evaluate, e.g. '[age] >= 18 and [consent] = "1"'

event.description: Event name (optional, for longitudinal projects only)

tools.name: survey.getLink
tools.description: Generate a survey link URL for a specific instrument and record. The instrument must be enabled as a survey in the project.

record_id.description: The record ID to generate the survey link for

instrument.description: The instrument machine name (must be survey-enabled)

event.description: Event name (optional, for longitudinal projects only)

tools.name: records.save
tools.description: Create a new record or update an existing record in a REDCap project. The data object must include the record ID field. Use projects.getMetadata first to learn the field names and types before saving.

data.description: Record data object with field_name: value pairs. Must include the record ID field (typically 'record_id').

overwrite.description: If true, overwrite existing values. If false (default), only save to empty fields.
